claim: For every finite alphabet \(A\), every \(k\ge 2\), and every unbordered word \(u\in A^k\), let \(\widehat{\mathcal F}(k,u)\) be Pribavkina's \(2k\)-state completed semi-flower automaton for \(A^k\setminus\{u\}\), with state set \(Q=\{0,1,\ldots,2k-1\}\). For \(0\le r\le k-1\), the minimum length of a word \(w\) satisfying \(|Qw|\le k-r\) is exactly \(k+r(k+1)\). Equivalently, if \(\lambda_{k,u}(s)=\min\{|w|:|Qw|\le 2k-s\}\), then \(\lambda_{k,u}(s)=k+(s-k)(k+1)\) for every \(k\le s\le 2k-1\). For every letter \(a\in A\), the word \(u(au)^r\) has length \(k+r(k+1)\) and image rank exactly \(k-r\).
integrity: The all-parameter theorem is proved symbolically. Exhaustive power-automaton computations on 84 binary and 216 ternary unbordered words are supporting checks only and are not used to infer the infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The theorem determines only the high-deficiency range from rank k through rank 1. Thresholds for ranks above k can depend on the internal letter pattern of the unbordered word u. Originality remains subject to the residual possibility of an older equivalent formulation under incomplete-set or transformation-rank terminology.
title: Exact high-deficiency rank profile of Pribavkina's \(\widehat{\mathcal F}(k,u)\) automata
